record.prompt: Our API gateway runs 4 worker processes (deploy/server.conf) and limits each API key to 100 requests a minute in gateway/limits.py. Read https://docs.quillon.example/config and tell me whether a key really gets 100 per minute overall, or more.
record.final_answer:
A key can get more than 100 per minute. In the worst case it gets up to **400 per minute**, and up to about 800 in any rolling 60 seconds.

**Why:**

- `gateway/limits.py` builds `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` without setting a `backend`. The Quillon 1.8 docs say the default backend is `memory`, where each process keeps its own counters. They state that "an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate." We pin `quillon==1.8.2`, so those docs apply.
- `deploy/server.conf` sets `workers = 4`. Each worker lets a key make 100 requests, so the key can make 400 a minute in total. How close a client gets to 400 depends on how the server spreads requests across workers, but a client sending a lot of traffic will get near it.
- Windows are fixed and reset at the start of each clock minute. That means a key can use its full allowance at the end of one minute and again at the start of the next. Across the 4 workers, that's up to about 800 requests in roughly 60 seconds.

**Fix:** switch to the shared backend so all workers use one counter:

```python
limiter = Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key", backend="tally", url="tally://<host>:7070")
```

This needs a tallyd server that every worker can reach. Even then, the fixed window still allows up to about 200 requests around a minute boundary, and the docs don't mention a sliding-window option. A quicker stopgap is to set the rate to 25/minute per worker, which adds up to 100 overall. That only works if requests are spread evenly across workers, and it would refuse legitimate requests when they aren't.

I haven't changed any code.
